app: Structured- Daily Planner Todo - Visual Calendar & Organizer
text: Good but free version is lacking . It's a good app with a nice UI and is fairly intuitive, but I'm really disappointed in fairly basic features being paywalled. I'm a student looking to use an app for tracking daily class schedules and blocking out study time, but the fact that the ability to repeat events is locked behind the pro version disappoints me greatly. I know that it's probably a smaller team independently making the app but making repeated events paywalled makes this app useless for students that don't want to be burdened with yet another subscription fee or pay a whopping $100 one-time payment. The other option is to tediously manually enter in repeating events every day, but who would bother to do that every single day? I have ADHD and was looking for an app to help manage my time and scheduling and having to input every repeating event manually is not feasible for me. Unfortunate since I thought this might actually be an app that could help, but I guess I have to go back to searching.

app: Structured- Daily Planner Todo - Visual Calendar & Organizer
text: Useless without a subscription . This app is probably great with a subscription, its cute, well designed, and I do like the visual aspect of it. However, I have ADHD and NEED reminders of tasks at least 5-30 minutes beforehand- but without the subscription this app only notifies you AT the exact time you should be starting the task. Additionally, the timer on the task starts whether or not you actually open the app, so often by the time I've prepared myself to start the task, the time window has ended. I'm sure I could circumvent these issues by scheduling in time to prepare for the task, but it just irritates me that I have to work around what is normally a very basic function in any planning app. Other apps I've used allow you to choose one reminder a chosen time before the task, but additional reminders require a subscription. If this was the case with Structured I would have no issue with the other features behind a paywall. For example you can accommodate for repeat tasks being behind a paywall by duplicating tasks and scheduling them for different days. I completely understand that developers need to make money- but I'm simply better off using the reminders built into my phone since I do not have to pay for reminders. Perhaps for those without ADHD or who are already diligent planners, this would not be an issue! In that case I do recommend trying this app. It is cute and unique and I especially like the energy levels you can assign to each task.

text: I love it! . I was recently diagnosed with ADHD and was advised to literally add more “structure” to my day. text: I am a freelance artist with ADHD and this is perfect . I have such a hard time keeping consistent with my work and having a solid schedule bc it's 100% on me to keep on track. Having ADHD makes that HARD but I've gotta say, Structure has been a godsend. It's so well thought out, user friendly, and customizable. I LOVE that I can not only have my task list oranized down to the minute but a todo list WITHIN the task. And checking off those lil boxes just scratch my lil neurodivergent brain in the best way. I also LOVE the reminder box for the todos that I want to get done but don't have a specific timeslot for. I've used notion, google calendars, notes apps, planners, etc and this by far is my favorite and has everything I need in one place FOR FREE. Though, I may get the Pro version (One paymeny of like $9 which is honestly so worth it to me) because you can set it up so your schedule can easily repeat without having to manually input it daily. The only thing stopping me from getting the pro version rn is bc planning out my next day has become part of my nighttime routine that I am thoroughly enjoying since this is still so new to me. (I've had this app for about a week now). tldr; Get this app if you need some Structure in your life. It is so well thought out and helps me keep my ADHD brain on track.

text: issues . The overall app is quite useful. i have adhd and so struggle with time management and keeping routines, so this was very useful when i found it. text: Surprisingly effective . A friend suggested this to me and I new that I'd initially enjoy it and make use of it but I thought as per usual I'd become distracted, bored and forget it existed. I have adhd and very much struggle to motivate myself to do many tasks, with a bit of setting up I'm now finding I'mactually still doing things I'd normally have given up eg eating more veg with my meals, drinking more water and such. It works on the principle that you set yourself daily tasks which by completing you earn rainbow stones which are effectively the in game currency. You use these to buy room decorations, clothes and later on can buy other things like different colours for your finch and locations to visit. You also can connect to friends finches and send them things like hugs, compliments and so on through the day. There's also useful journeys which are groups of tasks that encourage you to do certain things eg feel more positive, eat more healthily and such. These contain suggested tasks but you can also add your own. As with anything you could frig the system if you wanted, earn lots of rainbow stones without actually doing anything but ultimately the only person you'd be cheating is yourself. The paid option goes towards keeping the app going for everyone (why I paid) and does unlock a few more slots in the randomly populated shop plus you get more seasonable achievements and some more task customisation options. However it's very good even as a free version. There's also an option to apply for a guardian to sponsor you paid membership if you can't afford it, which are generous people who pay extra per month so others can get more out of the app. There's a few bonuses for this but nothing significant, it's more about the desire to help other people. app: Tiimo- To-Do List Planner - Schedule Structured Daily Task
text: An absolute lifesaver for those with learning differences . I don't normally leave app reviews but if there's one app that deserves it it's Tiimo. Developing a routine and positive habits is a continuous challenge for me, and my as-yet-untreated ADHD has caused me to try almost every app on the App Store to organise myself. I somehow keep returning to Tiimo however, a year after I first signed up. Firstly, Tiimo has an incredibly user friendly interface, and it feels pleasant to use. There are lots of different icons available to visually distinguish between activities and tasks. On the premium membership, importing your calendar events is seamless. Several features really make Tiimo stand apart from other planning tools. Unlike just using Apple Calendar, for example, Tiimo has a timer view that allows you to only see what you're working on right now. For someone like me that is prone to distraction this is critical. No other apps seem to implement this in the same way as Tiimo. Another feature is that there are several different ‘levels' available for your activities and tasks. For example, you could have a single activity as it's own timer, or if you're working on something that has lots of steps you can use checklists that sit below a particular activity. Activities themselves can be combined as part of routines that themselves can be saved, set to repeat and so on. I've found the most effective mornings I've had over the past year have been ones where I have all my morning activities laid out for me in advance and I can just move my way through the timers. Otherwise I never get anywhere! As a final point, the app is specifically designed for folks with specific challenges, be this ASD, ADHD, and so on, and as such I find it fits my brain really well. Knowing that this user base is in mind in every step of the design process is fantastic, and I believe the team deserve all the credit for their hard work. They're also incredibly open to suggestions and feedback, and the subscription price I feel is incredibly reasonable for an app that you can use every single day, all day long, for all manner of uses. It particularly shines when used in conjunction with a smart watch (e.g. the Apple Watch) as I can leave my phone somewhere else as I just follow the timers on my wrist. I could keep going so I'll stop here! Thank you for developing Tiimo - the community feels so supportive and positive and it's brought a little bit of light into my life while I've been navigating receiving an ADHD diagnosis as an adult.

app: TimeFinder- Daily Planner - Time Blocking, Hourly Schedule
text: Reduced my stress . love this app for keeping my sanity of which tasks to focus on and which to do another day. This app allows me to brain dump all my tasks into a list and then decide each day which ones to slide into my schedule. I can make todo lists for each work project and not have to write them on a separate calendar. In the paid version, it also syncs to your external calendar events by automatically blocking them in for you. It's reduced my stress because I frequently over fill my day from imagining I can do more. Now I can realistically know what I can do for that day by visually seeing a concrete plan of blocked tasks. It's so much better than just a list of tasks written into a calendar to fit in around meetings. And if I don't finish a task that day, it's easy to add it back into my schedule the next day. I can also see my progress on which tasks I've completed. So I can easily count up the hours spent on each project. I have a hard time estimating how long tasks take and by extending the time block and moving a task to the next day, I've been realizing how much I under estimate my time projections. No wonder I always feel behind. It's so easy to extend the time block for a task and move other tasks to a different time block. You can set up time blocks as small as 5 minutes. And you can drag over multiple tasks into one time block. I also want to add that the user interface is so simple and intuitive to use. It's great not to feel overwhelmed by features. It also syncs across all Mac devices for the paid version. And there are notifications for each time block. You can test out so many features in the free version. I paid for the premium version to sync my calendar and use over all my devices. The developer also takes feedback of feature requests and improves the app with them. I feel in command of my work schedule now. Having ADHD and difficulty with time management and with trouble getting started on tasks because my todo list seems overwhelming, it's been a life saver for me.

app: Tiimo- To-Do List Planner - Schedule Structured Daily Task
text: Unfortunately, not ADHD friendly . I'm just letting this warning here because it was nowhere to be found before I purchased the app: they REMOVED THE “ROUTINE” FUNCTION in some update, despite promoting this feature in all of their communications. That said, this really doesn't matter AS MUCH, since you can still create one activity called, let's say… “Morning Routine” and have subtasks on it. But as an ADHDer myself, this app has 2 flaws that I simply cannot understand, even more on an app that is made by and for us neurodivergents: 1) it “punishes” you if you are late for any activity 2) it does not allow to enter activities with a due date+time, but without a defined duration. Let me explain: 1) ALL activities have an individual and automatic timer, that starts at the due date/time an it is great to be able to see the activity and the time passing by in real time WHEN YOU CAN MAKE IT ON TIME. Because if you, for some reason are late, you CANNOT STOP IT, or even edit it. Only pause it. Also, if you accidentally tap on the “play” button right above an activity, you cannot undo it. For both cases (activity already started or accidentally tap on “play” button), you have to delete the activity and re-insert it! Let me give an example: I had a swimming class today on my Google Calendar at 10AM but the teacher couldn't make it and just told me after 10AM. Tiimo has an integration with GC, so it imported the event, but right at 10pm the timer started to roll until 11am, automatically! You cannot edit ANY event, the imported and/or the ones we create originally in app, AFTER it starts. I wrote an email about all I'm writing here, and they've confirmed: I have to DELETE the activity and re-insert it again, with the new date/time. And if the activity was imported from GC, I have to go out of the app, go to Google Calendar, delete and re-enter the event with the new date+time. That's more time wasting and more opportunities to make mistakes and forget things… 2) Another big flaw for me is that we cannot create activities/events without a defined duration. Let's say I want to wash my dishes at 2PM, but I don't know how much time it takes yet. We all know “time blindness” is a struggle for us with ADHD and Autism! But in this app, instead, I have to create an activity on the day I want and leave it as “any time of the day” option, and remember that I need to do it by 2PM myself. That's right, a planning app in which you have to use your own memory (and we all know how bad our memories are, that's why we look for apps in the first place)… They give us another workaround, that is to create the “washing dishes” task with an approximate duration and DURING THE ACTIVITY, keep tapping the “+” icon to add more minutes. With my hands wet?! And if I was on my swimming class and it was longer than it usually is? I have to leave the pool running and go to the app to add more time before the class ends? How frustrating it is, to set an arbitrary time for something, like “editing a video”, and have to pause the activity itself to get the phone and keep adding minutes? How distracting and disappointing it is? So, basically, I need to pay for this app and for another one like Toggl to first track the time I take to do every single activity in my life and then use Tiimo. That doesn't make sense. And another consequence of this, is that I cannot have on the same app, my tasks/activities and basic reminders, like someone's birthday or holiday! If you import a “moon phase” or any calendar I just mentioned to Tiimo that is just an reminder for the day (and not a task per se), you have to set a timing duration or it will be together with the “anytime” tasks during the day. I just don't understand… so now I have to pay for Tiimo, Toggl and have to leave the app and enter on my Calendar app to see “all day” events that aren't tasks, like “credit card due date”, or “Easter”. That's the perfect recipe for failure as someone who struggles with focus and attention! _ So, to summarize, on Tiimo, I have the following results by the end of my day: • A swimming lesson that I supposedly did, but in reality didn't; • A pile of dishes in the sink, that I now have to wash in the evening when I am out of energy and tired, because I couldn't guess the duration, so the task went to the “anytime” tab, that was closed to avoid distractions from the main ones; • A full afternoon supposedly without any activity, because I needed to use another app to track the time I took to edit a video, so that I can add it more accurately on Tiimo the next time; • Oh, and I forgot to call my friend on her birthday, because I couldn't add this event on Tiimo without a task attached to it and didn't entered my Calendar app today _ I know the creator's intentions are good, so I don't plan on lashing out here. I really have tried the workarounds, but all I did was waste my money and patience. I'll be testing Tick-Tick now, since they have all the functions mentioned, a minimalist layout and widgets way more useful!

app: Structured- Daily Planner Todo - Visual Calendar & Organizer
text: Amazing if you need someone to tell you when to start/stop things . I live with treatment resistant bipolar I, and because it is treatment resistant I've had to make significant lifestyle changes to help manage it and prevent mood episodes. One of these changes (and one of the most important ones at that) is by implementing and sticking to strict routines. Mood episodes are often caused by variances in your sleep/wake cycle, so that's part of it- but having a strict routine also alerts other people near you when something is wrong because it's much easier to tell when you're not okay/starting an episode. One issue though, is that I also have ADHD and I can't take anything for it because the medication triggers mania for me. Time constantly gets away from me and I end up sitting in one spot for 10 hours and yet not even finding time for mundane things like brushing my teeth- for a long time I've felt like I've just been going in circles- I get nothing done all day, so I can't sleep at correct times because there are things I HAVE to get done, mood episode triggers, interventions cause even more disruption to normal living, hospital staff establishes routines, get better, rinse and repeat. My therapist recently recommended using an app or alarms to track my day and keep things moving along- I looked at a lot but so many are very expensive and don't even offer much. I downloaded this one because it has a lifetime purchase option of $30 or a month at $3 (or year at $10)- this is perfectly reasonable. While I don't think apps should be free because they take time, energy and money to make (and developers deserve to be paid for this)- I also didn't want to pay a lot for something that may not even work for me; my bipolar already costs me enough as is. I didn't try the free features, so I can't speak to those- but I love this app. I didn't realize how much having something remind me to to start/stop even just basic little things would make such a difference. I've only been using it for a month, but I've gotten so much stuff done that I'm actually impressed with myself. I'm fully caught up at work, my house is clean, I'm showering and brushing my teeth at correct intervals, I'm even reading again and taking nice walks with my dog. I always thought I was just incredibly lazy and would beat myself up over it even while my therapist tried to explain that I just lacked a proper sense of passing time and I'm finally starting to understand that. You can get so much stuff done a day if you just plan it and stick to it! I used to make decisions like “should I brush my teeth, shower, take a walk or get caught up on work today?” Like I could only do one task at all on any given day. I haven't felt so proud of myself in so long, even if it's just for functional like a normal human being- but this app has honestly been a lifesaver for me. I also love the calendar sync features because I can sync all my work meetings and personal obligations right into my schedule. The only thing I currently wish the app could do is allow me to just swap two tasks. It would also be nice if there was a type of report you could see that tracked things you didn't click off so you can start to understand why you might have been missing stuff (maybe two tasks need to be spread out- maybe one takes longer than you think, etc). But now I just do whatever my Apple Watch says I should be doing, whether it's reading, working, eating, showering or just relaxing- and my life is actually looking a lot brighter.

app: TickTick-To-Do List & Calendar - Task remind, planner,countdown
text: One App to Rule Them All . OMG this app is so good I had to write an essay about it. It does so many things but the interface is so clean, it's kind of a design miracle. I can do everything I need in the free version but I subscribed because I want this app to exist forever. I have ADHD, so I'm always strategizing to manage my focus. Someone on an ADHD forum recommended TickTick and with some hesitation (oh no not another system…), I downloaded it a few weeks ago. I like productivity apps but if i have to flip between them, it's not useful for me because … squirrel. TickTick has replaced the following apps for me: - ToDoist, Google Tasks - Done (habit tracker) - Toggl (task timer) - Notion (Notion is still awesome for many things, just not project management for my brain) - GoodNotes (ditto - still awesome, just not for tracking stuff) - and any number of timers and to-do lists TickTick takes my to-do list and puts the information in front of me when I need it. I can filter to just the things I need to immediately handle. I can set it to show me how long I have until the next thing is due (very helpful for a brain that only understands Now and Not Now.) It brings in my calendar events so I can see my days in context. I can start a Pomodoro (timed focus session) from within the task itself. It tracks habits and streaks, allowing me to write notes if I want to. When I reach a goal, it shows cute little animations that I like, (and I usually hate cute little animations.) And it's got robust widgets, so good that I actually use the Apple Watch app. I actually use it on every device I own, iPad, Watch, Phone, as well as my PC via Chrome. Anyway if you are still reading, just get this app. It's amazing. Thank you for coming to my Ted Talk.

app: ADHD Schedule Planner- Weel - Calendar & Schedule Organizer
text: Actually represents time in an ADHD-friendly way . I'm in the trial period, so I have a few days to decide whether to purchase a subscription, but here are my thoughts so far. I have been looking so long for something that will tell me how long it is until the next event that I've been seriously considering learning Xcode/Swift so I could write my own application. My ADHD brain looks at "appointment at 15:30" and just shrugs. I then have to check the current time, and do some mental math.. which is just enough effort that I'm likely to simply make a bad assumption about how long I have instead, and anyway the whole process just needlessly adds mental friction when all I ever want to know is how long until the thing. This app will tell you "2h 20m". Yes! No mental effort needed to interpret, no additional information to look up. I know how long I have. And the widgets and watch complications represent time this way as well. Perfect. Another positive: the wheel. It does just make more sense to me. It's easier to scan and understand where I am and how much time various things will take. And it's nice for time blocking because you can just move stuff around the circle when you get off track and need to push some things until later. AND it actually updates the entries in your actual calendar when you update them on the circle (except in one case, which I'll mention in a moment). Oh, and you can "dim" calendars that you still want to see but that aren't vital to you. I tried using a similar app with a round interface, Owaves, and loved it. Its UI was definitely smoother, but it was a complete walled garden with no way to sync events to other calendars and they were trying to push people to use it as social media, which makes me suspicious that they're just going to end up funding it with your data. I prefer Pical's approach. And regarding the privacy aspect: there's no account to sign up for, the dev claims not to collect your data, it uses calendars you already have (for me that's my iOS and Nextcloud calendars), so you keep control of your data while it keeps itself synced across your devices. Excellent. Those are some major positives. Here are the negatives: - The widgets and interface don't automatically change with system dark/light mode. The light mode is easier to read, but at night a bright screen is a problem for me, so I have to keep manually turning it on and off. Annoying. - If you create an event in the app you can't assign it to a calendar, so it will only ever appear in the app and not on your other calendars. If you want an event to sync, you have to create it elsewhere. - The wheel is shaded between 6am and 6pm for night time/day time, and you can't change it. For me that time is completely arbitrary, so it only adds distracting visual noise. It would be better to leave out the shading until the ability to customise it is added. - Sometimes moving events and deleting events can be glitchy. I assume this is from the overhead needed to update your external calendars as well, but it makes the app feel a bit clunky. - Price. It's kind of spendy. On the one hand, I prefer to pay developers so they don't need to monetize via data mining. But they're charging 3 times the cost of Fantastical for a subscription. It's a bit much. Mitigating these negatives is the fact that the developer has the roadmap on their website, and the app appears to be getting at least a couple of updates a month, so it's actively being worked on. All in all I'm thrilled that someone is actually making a calendar app tailored to my brain, and I'm hopeful that it will continue to get improvements.

text: Amazing . Got this app a few weeks ago and it's been helping me with my WFH ADHD. Helps me stay focus when studying and reminding me when to mediate with a timer and alarm! I like how you can put different tags on the habits, it makes it easier to focus on the important tasks. I couldn't figure out what the difference was between free & premium. After a week, I decided just to pay the $4.99 in case my data doesn't back up in the cloud. Plus that's the price for a lifetime. It's a great app and it deserves every penny.

app: Finch - Self-Care Pet - Daily Journal & Habit Tracker
text: finch has an impact . I've been using this app for almost a year now, and I haven't missed a single day. That's HUGE! I've never been anywhere close to this consistent with any self-care/habit-tracker app before. I've managed to stay mostly functional with various issues (depression, autism, ADHD) my entire life, but like many others things took a bad turn for me during the pandemic. This app made a huge difference in my day-to-day quality of life, and that's after trying numerous other apps, self-help books, online suppor groups, and what little therapy my insurance provided ran dry. THIS app is what helps me get out of bed on the really tough days, and it's been there for me for 350+ days and counting. A couple features I want to highlight: 1. they introduced an option to back up saves on a server I think, BUT it can be saved locally (on your phone) so you never have to worry about deeply personal health info or journaling being sold to advertisers, ending up in the wrong hands due to hacking, or the company caving to unethical search warrants. Privacy matters a lot to me (it should matter to everyone!) and the Finch team appears to have put real consideration into protecting their users instead of just offering the platitudes and disclaimers that are unfortunately common. 2. this may be the most LGBTQIA+ friendly app I've ever used. No small part of my distress over the last couple years has been from watching the hateful and dangerous backlash against people on the margins, and I don't think I could handle using an app made for comfort that constantly reminded me it was built exclusively with cishet people in mind… and yes, I've used apps that make a weirdly big deal out of gender and sexuality. Why does a journaling or habit app, for example, need to categorize me as man or woman? Why does an affirmations app need to assume I'm waiting for love, and specifically and exclusively from the “opposite sex”? The weird obsession with promoting the cishet lifestyle crops up in surprising places on other apps, but Finch doesn't make a big deal of any of that and just lets me be me. That means a lot.

app: Loop Habit Tracker

As a bonus, you get great backup functions. I can't imagine managing every day without this anymore. Thank you to all the individuals who helped make this app!

app: TickTick-To-Do List & Calendar - Task remind, planner,countdown
text: The best thing that has ever happened to me . As someone with severe ADHD, executive functioning has always been a major struggle for me, making it difficult to get things done. app: TimeTune - Schedule Planner

app: Finch - Self-Care Pet - Daily Journal & Habit Tracker
text: some (very friendly) suggestions . i never write reviews, but felt compelled to for this amazing little birdie self care app. i have severe adhd, like a lot of other users, and this is the only app i've ever stuck with. it truly means something special when i write my very first app store review ever because i love this app so much that ive invested a ton of thought into ways to make it even better and cooler. every day that i greet my birdie, poppy, i think of new ways to improve her life and enrich her experiences. here's some of my ideas!! - my favorite part of the app is definitely the clothing and furniture you're awarded or buy, and i think it would be awesome if you expand it a bit more! i'd love to see location specific furniture items, because i love the locational clothing items so much. - also, i feel like finishing a location is a bit lackluster right now - perhaps awarding a special micropet (or unlocking the collection from the first square in the clothing store) when you complete a location? - i also love the mood breakdown - it would be awesome if i could export my data somehow to excel; i'm a sociology major and think it would be so interesting to analyze in a research setting. thank you for creating such a phenomenal app!!!

app: Tiimo- To-Do List Planner - Schedule Structured Daily Task
text: Unfortunately, not ADHD friendly . I'm just letting this warning here because it was nowhere to be found before I purchased the app: they REMOVED THE “ROUTINE” FUNCTION in some update, despite promoting this feature in all of their communications. That said, this really doesn't matter AS MUCH, since you can still create one activity called, let's say… “Morning Routine” and have subtasks on it. But as an ADHDer myself, this app has 2 flaws that I simply cannot understand, even more on an app that is made by and for us neurodivergents: 1) it “punishes” you if you are late for any activity 2) it does not allow to enter activities with a due date+time, but without a defined duration. Let me explain: 1) ALL activities have an individual and automatic timer, that starts at the due date/time an it is great to be able to see the activity and the time passing by in real time WHEN YOU CAN MAKE IT ON TIME. Because if you, for some reason are late, you CANNOT STOP IT, or even edit it. Only pause it. Also, if you accidentally tap on the “play” button right above an activity, you cannot undo it. For both cases (activity already started or accidentally tap on “play” button), you have to delete the activity and re-insert it! Let me give an example: I had a swimming class today on my Google Calendar at 10AM but the teacher couldn't make it and just told me after 10AM. Tiimo has an integration with GC, so it imported the event, but right at 10pm the timer started to roll until 11am, automatically! You cannot edit ANY event, the imported and/or the ones we create originally in app, AFTER it starts. I wrote an email about all I'm writing here, and they've confirmed: I have to DELETE the activity and re-insert it again, with the new date/time. And if the activity was imported from GC, I have to go out of the app, go to Google Calendar, delete and re-enter the event with the new date+time. That's more time wasting and more opportunities to make mistakes and forget things… 2) Another big flaw for me is that we cannot create activities/events without a defined duration. Let's say I want to wash my dishes at 2PM, but I don't know how much time it takes yet. We all know “time blindness” is a struggle for us with ADHD and Autism! But in this app, instead, I have to create an activity on the day I want and leave it as “any time of the day” option, and remember that I need to do it by 2PM myself. That's right, a planning app in which you have to use your own memory (and we all know how bad our memories are, that's why we look for apps in the first place)… They give us another workaround, that is to create the “washing dishes” task with an approximate duration and DURING THE ACTIVITY, keep tapping the “+” icon to add more minutes. With my hands wet?! And if I was on my swimming class and it was longer than it usually is? I have to leave the pool running and go to the app to add more time before the class ends? How frustrating it is, to set an arbitrary time for something, like “editing a video”, and have to pause the activity itself to get the phone and keep adding minutes? How distracting and disappointing it is? So, basically, I need to pay for this app and for another one like Toggl to first track the time I take to do every single activity in my life and then use Tiimo. That doesn't make sense. And another consequence of this, is that I cannot have on the same app, my tasks/activities and basic reminders, like someone's birthday or holiday! If you import a “moon phase” or any calendar I just mentioned to Tiimo that is just an reminder for the day (and not a task per se), you have to set a timing duration or it will be together with the “anytime” tasks during the day. I just don't understand… so now I have to pay for Tiimo, Toggl and have to leave the app and enter on my Calendar app to see “all day” events that aren't tasks, like “credit card due date”, or “Easter”. That's the perfect recipe for failure as someone who struggles with focus and attention! _ So, to summarize, on Tiimo, I have the following results by the end of my day: • A swimming lesson that I supposedly did, but in reality didn't; • A pile of dishes in the sink, that I now have to wash in the evening when I am out of energy and tired, because I couldn't guess the duration, so the task went to the “anytime” tab, that was closed to avoid distractions from the main ones; • A full afternoon supposedly without any activity, because I needed to use another app to track the time I took to edit a video, so that I can add it more accurately on Tiimo the next time; • Oh, and I forgot to call my friend on her birthday, because I couldn't add this event on Tiimo without a task attached to it and didn't entered my Calendar app today _ I know the creator's intentions are good, so I don't plan on lashing out here. I really have tried the workarounds, but all I did was waste my money and patience. I'll be testing Tick-Tick now, since they have all the functions mentioned, a minimalist layout and widgets way more useful!

app: Tiimo- To-Do List Planner - Schedule Structured Daily Task
text: Can be very helpful, but very buggy and learning curve is not great . I've really enjoyed this app and it has helped me out a lot. However, the rigidity of it is very unhelpful for people with ADHD. I don't know if this is a feature and my app is buggy, or if you simply can't uncheck activities. Sometimes I'll accidentally check an activity off in a routine and I can't uncheck it! I'll have to start the whole routine over to get back. This also affects when I go in and add something to a routine already in progress, since tiimo will suddenly skip me like 3 activities. I was barely on my 3rd activity, added one to my routine, and it skipped me to like the 6th. And of course, I couldn't uncheck the checked activities, so I had to go and delete the routine, add it back, and start it over. I also wish we could add more time to an activity already happening. My time blindness makes it hard to figure out how long something will take me, and when I realize something will take me longer than I thought, I have to pause the activity and use an external timer, which mixes me up! Being able to restart an activity already in progress would be good too (sometimes I get distracted and can't start exactly when it wants, but seeing it already started discourages me from getting back on track. I also think that the learning curve is very large, the initial app instructions are vague, and the blog posts linked are too many and too long with not enough screenshots just to get a barebones understanding how the app works. I've had more help watching youtubers use it than from the tutorials they have. I totally understand this is a work in progress, and I will continue to support the team of course. This has helped me get on track and balance my life much better. But the inflexibility is really frustrating and discouraging.

app: Brili Routines – Habit Tracker - ADHD Planner Grow & Thrive
text: Fantastic concept with imperfect execution . After only a few days I can say that so far, this has been a super effective and helpful tool for me, and I am actually considering purchasing a subscription when the trial is up (which is a huge deal for me because I generally do not purchase subscriptions for apps, unless it is something that is particularly useful for me). However, I have found a few things that are buggy or not quite as convenient as I would have hoped, which is the reason I give this product 4 stars rather than 5. Concept/overall effectiveness of this type of tool for me: 5 stars (not to be dramatic but to say it's been potentially life-changing after a pretty short time may be appropriate) Execution/app design: 4 stars - there are a few things that I think could be a little more convenient or user-centric but overall pretty good Programming: maybe 3.5 stars - I've found a few things that are a little buggy or picky about the movements required to execute a particular task. I'm not a professional programmer, but I have a degree in electrical engineering and I've programmed various things. I'm not overly impressed with the programming compared to similar apps or even feel like I could have programmed it better (realizing that it may be harder to get some of the features right than I'm envisioning, but I'm still not impressed). Price point/value: 4 stars (not based on comparing it to other available stuff, but just the value for the product itself based on cost per year feels slightly higher than I would like to see both from the perspective of being on a student budget, terms of affordability or financial accessibility for more people who would benefit from this, but overall not too bad and I am considering purchasing a subscription if I don't find an alternative similar product that works almost as well for my needs. It would be nice to see different “tiers” for different budgets as well - for example basic or intermediate versions that you can purchase for different prices that perhaps limit the number of routines and/or routine tasks you can enter with the pro or unlimited version available for people with the budget for the full subscription fee. Overall great app, but I would like to see various improvements, such as making the swiping for tasks less sensitive, an “undo” option to bring a completed or deleted task back, ability to create subroutines or break tasks down into subtasks for worse brain days, reorder a bunch of tasks on the list more efficiently in the middle of a routine or add/delete tasks from the routine list for the current day during the routine, change the time limit for a tasks or whether you earn the stars for a task during the routine or afterward, edit your star total or stars earned by adding or subtracting manually, “choose your adventure” style forks in the routine, set in advance optional tasks and whether or not a task can be skipped or done in less time if you're running late (e.g. I want to be able to set minimum and maximum time estimates for the routine or tasks that can be done faster, and if I woke up late I want to be able to have presets/settings that I can easily see and change where the app knows I can either rush through breakfast and a shower or skip them, skip playing with my cat and doing Duolingo, but I can't skip driving to work or make it take less time, etc.) The current system just tries to make every task take a much shorter time without adjusting the end time, and this is not always practical. The concept of tasks in the routine and the timers is amazing and very helpful, but beyond that it doesn't feel like the features are as well designed for adults with ADHD to use on the fly as I would like. It does seem to have been overly impacted in its design by the original app that was designed for parents to manage their children's routines, rather than designed for adults with ADHD to manage their own routines.

app: ADHD Schedule Planner- Weel - Calendar & Schedule Organizer

app: Streaks - The habit-forming to-do list
text: Love this!! . I'm a grown up with responsibilities and expectations... But my little ADHD self STILL forgets to brush my teeth at night. I have gotten out of bed to brush my teeth just because I didn't want to lose my streak. I would be giving it a 5, except sometimes I accidentally put a habit as being done and it's difficult to undo it once you've marked it done. It that was easier to alter, I'd give this a 5!

app: Fabulous - Daily Habit Tracker - Morning Routines & ADHD Help
text: Just some random person who used a little bit the app . I really hope the devs would read my review. app: RoutineFlow - Routine for ADHD
text: Edit: Please please please make an undo delete option. I made an intensely long chore list and somehow my brain thought to delete instead of duplicate. My ADD/ADHD makes routines tough. I've tried lists but they never work out well. This app helps me improve my focus, makes me feel like what I'm doing takes me significantly less time than what I estimate (if I feel a task will take me forever, I'll avoid doing it.) What can be improved is the ability to sort routines for the day.

app: Focus Keeper - Pomodoro Timer - ADHD Organizer & Productivity
text: Add “edit, delete, or adjust” options . The app is very nice, but it happened to me twice that I forgot to stop the timer and it counted me 22h of work. I can't delete or edit it, which affects my weekly statistics and adds the work that I haven't done. Also, if you forget to mark your habit as „done”, everything for the previous day gets blocked the next day. Having adhd means you often forget things, so it would be helpful to be able to edit the previous day or adjust the extra time added to your focus session.

app: Todoery- To Do List & Planner
text: I enjoy this app. It has been helping me to get things done more often - the visual is great for my ADHD, and the check box system is a nice dopamine hit lol. These personally would be useful for me so that I can reflect back on a day where I felt less motivated. Otherwise, it's a good simple little app.

app: Finch - Self-Care Pet - Daily Journal & Habit Tracker
text: Not ADHD or Night Owl Friendly . I downloaded this app because I have ADHD and find it hard to keep up with tasks. So far, it's very cute. However, I hate that we're not able to edit or see past days' progress. If there is a way to do so, it's not very obvious or accessible. The clock is also not in sync with my time zone (PST). I tried to check off tasks from my list around 11 pm and saw that the app already moved onto the next day! It felt kinda invalidating and as if I was being punished for not living at “normal” hours. The UI feels very overwhelming for someone who is already scattered.

app: Fabulous - Daily Habit Tracker - Morning Routines & ADHD Help
text: New Updates Make it Difficult to Navigate and Easy to Give Up . I used to have this app a few years ago and I LOVED it. It really helped me develop habits I wanted to start - and suggested new ones I hadn't thought of. Life has changed a lot (marriage, moving, new job) and I've fallen off the bandwagon with some of those habits so I decided to redownload. I really want to like this app but it is just too complicated. My adhd brain gets really distracted by all of their resources on my habits page. I can't figure out how to really use the app because there are so many resources and tabs..I don't mind resources but I feel like there needs to be clear separation so I can engage with them when I WANT to. It's also difficult to go back and “check off” a habit from a previous day if I forgot to check it off the day before. I also found their social page a bit disingenuous…many people who struggle with building habits struggle with distraction. Creating app features that encourage people to stay on the app, scroll and engage, instead of go out and live their life with their new habits feels so counterproductive. Unfortunately I got overwhelmed after 4 days. Please simplify the habits page and I would tell all my friends!

app: Fabulous - Daily Habit Tracker - Morning Routines & ADHD Help
text: Forgets progress - defeating, confusing, expensive . I was really excited to start using this and have never paid this much for an app before. Ever. I thought I was investing in my future. Not only is this app extremely confusing to use, and doesn't give solid reminders, but it has no way to go back and check off that you completed something the day prior, so it starts your “journey” over as if you didn't do what you were supposed to do because you didn't physically go into the app, which isn't great for ADHD - it needs to be more easily accessible with the ability to change past progress on busy days. On top of this, the app forgets that you already checked something off for the day. Today, not only did it forget that I had already checked off the first two items of the day, and made me do it again, but when I check the items off once more, it started me back at day one of my journey, and that is not accurate at all. The whole point is to help you see the progress you're making to keep you motivated, but if it can't keep track of your progress, it makes you feel like you aren't getting anywhere, and if it's too difficult to figure out how to check things off in the first place, the result is the same… It's so incredibly discouraging and I'm very upset that I have spent money on this. If it was an investment that helped me in my life, it would be so worth it. But I would've been better off setting alarms and using a paper checklist or journal, which Is what we're trying to avoid, right? Oh, and the amount of ads for slightly different apps by the same company is insulting and makes you feel used like the company is just trying to make money and doesn't actually care about helping the customer, which… the rest of my experience communicates as well. On another note, the music send to play randomly and is difficult to control even when the app is closed! Lastly, there needs to be better proofreading. There are so many spelling and grammatical errors. The low level of quality for writing or even quoted citations is absolutely unacceptable at this price. This has been a deeply frustrating experience.

app: Fabulous - Daily Habit Tracker - Morning Routines & ADHD Help
text: ADHD help . After trying several habit apps, this one was by far the best about getting me to establish habits slowly and SUSTAINABLY. Of course my natural way was to try to change everything at once… I like that this has coaching and encourages you do just do one bit at a time. There are a few things I would improve about the app (like a section for notes or brain dumps and the ability to edit previous days) but the developers are actively taking feedback which is great

app: Me+ Lifestyle Routine - Daily Planner & Habit Tracker

My only real gripe is adding water to my daily intake. For some unexplainable reason I can not add water the next morning to the previous days intake. There are nights I just don't get to it so my levels are totally off and unreliable, therefore just useless to me.

app: Me+ Lifestyle Routine - Daily Planner & Habit Tracker
text: Almost there! But some issues . I've been using this app for a few weeks, my mom is paying for my premium subscription and also has it on her phone. The app is great, it's been helping me keep track of my habits because I have ADHD and struggle with productivity, it also documents daily mood stats and reflections, every night I look forward to opening the app and checking off what I've done and reflecting on my day and documenting my mood. However I've had some issues, two days ago I opened the app and saw that all of my habits had disappeared and my habit stats disappeared too, I had to manually re-add all my habits and apparently my original habits aren't completely gone because when I tried to re-add one of them it tells me that the habit already exists, but is nowhere to be found. My mood stats were untouched and still there, but that brings me to my next issue. When it hits 12 am, you can't go back to add your mood stat from the day before, you can go back on previous days in your habit stats to check off things you forgot to check off in the moment, but with mood stats you can't do that, so if you forgot to document your mood for the day and it hits 12 then you're out of luck. It's my biggest pet peeve with this app, sometimes I don't have the time/don't remember to check things off immediately, it isn't an issue with the habit stats but with mood stats you can't do anything about it. Overall it's a great app and I'll continue using it despite its minor issues, I just hope my previously stated problem gets solved because my habits from the past 2 weeks are completely gone! (I saw a data repair button at the bottom of the profile tab, but when I clicked it nothing seemed to change so I'm not sure what that's supposed to do)

app: Routine Planner, Habit Tracker - Daily Time Management for ADHD

app: PlanMe - Daily Routine Planner

app: RoutineFlow - Routine for ADHD
