app: Super Planner- ADHD Routine AI
text: This app doesn't help my ADHD. It judges me. Instead of reducing my mental load it increases it, telling me I have 25 unfinished tasks. I'm behind. I can't even have a day off without being told I must do more, a message I've received for a lifetime. I want freedom, but this feels like tyranny. I want to live in the now, not be constantly nagged about past/future. I'll be uninstalling this app, and I'm not prepared to discuss or debate my views. My views are mine. This app is not for me.

app: Finch - Self-Care Pet - Daily Journal & Habit Tracker
text: Feedback . Love the app. As a person struggling with severe adhd its hard to keep up with basic tasks. This app allowed me to turn those boring everyday tasks into game. Taking care of this little bird is fun. Even without subscription. However I would definitely subscribed if they added “sick day” or “off day”. I m currently sick with a flu and all regular tasks don't make sense because im literally surviving thru the fever and the symptoms. Now, I have this habit to take care of the bird pet but those few days don't make sense to even login into app. If the development team could create an extra step from “how you feel today” then if its bad “why?” And then “would you like to delete all the tasks for today?”. That would help a lot. Also that would make the app even better if you could choose a pet. Like cat, dog, unicorn horse etc. I don't really care about birds. But still love the app:) Thank you guys for an amazing app.

app: Fabulous - Daily Habit Tracker - Morning Routines & ADHD Help
text: Great….but… . So, honest review of the adhd and habit tracking apps. I was enjoying them until this morning. I had a “burnt out day” and slept until 1:00 pm. So I didn't complete my morning routine and now I feel like a complete failure at life. There's like no way to skip a day or even enter in that you had a down day and weren't able to complete your morning routine. It doesn't allow for the physical aspects that some mental health diagnoses bring. And now I have an app on my phone telling me I failed today. It's like Mom is still right here with me. Deleting.

app: RoutineFlow - Routine for ADHD
text: Life changing. I don't have ADHD, but I do struggle with estimating how long tasks will take. This app has helped me better plan my days so that I can get more done. I feel more confident since I'm taking care of the important stuff day to day. Try this app! 2025 UPDATE: Revising this down to a 4 because I'm really missing a "vacation mode." Apparently many other, similar apps have this feature.

app: Routine Planner, Habit Tracker
text: This is so cool, but I'd love to see more rewards, like the app for kids 'brili' has, and the ability to either postpone or skip a habit as time demands. Brili has star rewards for completing tasks, and then kids trade them in for rewards. I'd like to see routinery do this for adults, because there are several things about brili that make it harder for adults to use on themselves. The thing is, adhd adults need that reward motivation. Please incorporate the reward structure into this great app!

app: dubbii- the body doubling app
text: I'm disabled, so I have other limitations on top of crippling ADHD, and this app has changed my life. This app drastically helps me mentally do daily tasks that most people don't think twice about. I love being able to pause a video or skip a step and come back to it later if need be. $6 a month for the subscription is 10 million percent worth it for me! And rich and Roxy are awesome to listen to! 1000/10 recommend

app: Habit Tracker - Goal Tracker & ADHD Planner
text: If you struggle to get things done . I use this for habit tracking and also to do list. Between having ADHD and occasional depression, this app helps habits and to do's not feel so overwhelming. I'm actually getting things done. You can pick certain days of the week of month, or just do a daily count for each habit. They even have vacation mode, you can also add tags to your habits so they are categorized. I absolutely love how organized this app is, they have truly thought of everything when it comes to habit tracking!

app: Habit Tracker - Goal Tracker & ADHD Planner
text: Wonderful app but could be better! . This is a great app when used consistently, but for someone who already has trouble forming habits and needs the assistance of an app that is difficult! That is why even minor issues with user experience can lead to a rapid decline in usage. There are so many things this app does right, miles above any other app that I've used, so I'll focus on what it does wrong for the sake of brevity: - The option for push notifications is fantastic! Great reminder! However, if I click on the APP and not the NOTIFICATION, and mark a task as complete, the notification still persists. This tends to A) make me ignore the notifications entirely, or B) accidentally delete notifications for tasks I haven't done, while swiping to delete notifications for tasks I have done. - The option to skip a task is great, and the fact that it still closes the ring for the day is a solid win! This encourages me to come back to the app even if I don't complete a task. However, it would be nice if there was also a “Reschedule” option; e.g. I have a habit reminder to do laundry every Saturday but sometimes I don't get to it until Sunday. My options see either: A) skip the task, and not track that it was completed, or B) ignore it until it's done on Sunday and then go back and mark Saturday as complete (possibly even adding a memo that it was done another day) but this incorrectly tracks it as being done saturday - Widgets! I wish there was the option to just check a task off on the widget instead of clicking the widget to open the app! What's the point of all these different widget options if they're all just informational and not interactive, corporate says it's the same picture! Overall the devs have clearly worked really hard on this app and it shows. Great features and infinite customizability. I just wish these few quality improvements were made the the UX because even though they're minor changes they can make a WORLD of difference for someone with attention deficit and difficulty forming habits.

app: Finch - Self-Care Pet - Daily Journal & Habit Tracker
text: Great app! (awesome for helping my silly little adhd brain get tasks done) . This app has genuinely helped me with quite a few goals, especially when it comes to drinking more water and remembering to actually socialise with the people I love, something that I sometimes forget to do due to ADHD and the meds I'm on. Currently have a 209 day streak! (Go me!!) and am really loving it Thank you to the creators of this app and to the person who recommended it to me ( a good friend of mine ) for providing a tool that's both fun and useful in a way that never feels condescending or awkward. I've tried somewhat similar things in the past but always ended up dreading udon them by the end since it felt like it was shaming me whenever I messed up, whether that be true or whether it was just in my head via the wording, but finch NEVER makes me feel like that! It never makes me feel guilty for not completing a goal or for my goals being too simple, and actually encourages having simple goals on days that are difficult as to not end up getting burnt out. That, as well as having the option to pause streaks for when you're busy or just can't handle using it at that time, really helped when my grandad passed as it was difficult to do my daily finch during the organisation of the funeral and such, but when all that was done I was able to go right back to it with no problem, and was able to write down my feelings on it and get a little reward for doing so! Something as silly as the idea of receiving a fun little hat or a new rug for my little bird friend can end up getting me to take care of myself, and honestly I think that's just what I've needed all this time. (Though as a suggestion, it would be pretty cool to have more complex goals as an option for organisations sake, such as multi-step goals or the ability to link goals to each other and that being a way of getting more points? Sometimes I'll end up with an easy goal and a complex goal and both will give me the same amount of points which always feels off 😭 might just be a me thing though and I'm sure the team behind it have reasons why this may not logistically work anyways haha)

app: Routine Planner, Habit Tracker - Daily Time Management for ADHD
text: Life changing Assistive tech . I have been using this app for 3 months now, and it helped me to change my lifestyle entirely. I have pretty bad ADHD and this app is the best in making me do my regular drill without having to think about what comes next. Like, no mental load at all! I use it every day, for morning and evening routines. It is really so great because it also narrates the tasks and times, so I don't need to be glued to the screen and can just get on with my business and it's okay if my head is in the clouds. It also helps that ticking tasks is animated and each has an icon. Elements of gamification work wonders with my weird brain. I am still not bored with it after 3 months, because when I feel the routine getting old, I just change it! Apart from making sure I locked the entrance door and switched off the gas every night, I also noticed that I spend much more time with things that matter to me as part of my routine. Tasks or times set apart for doing things that align with my values. It forced me to think about how I want to live life in general, and gave a shape to experiments with intentionality. I am seriously looking forward to starting every morning, because I will have little islands of peace and celebration programmed in, while also doing the essentials. The streaks also don't break if I skip tasks sometimes so users are protected from the perfectionism trap while being able to celebrate getting through the routine anyway. I am really grateful for the ad-free design (those would distract me a lot), but I also think the premium tier is affordable. I test a lot of habit management apps and this one is absolutely pro stuff, massive cheers to the developers and everyone that made it happen💚💚💚

app: Routine Planner, Habit Tracker
text: i use the free version. this is a useful way of labeling countdown timers and it really aids my focus. i recommend it to those with ADHD or executive dysfunction. i especially like the flexibility of starting a routine when i want to, and of skipping those tasks that are irrelevant on certain days but not others, or are completed but i forgot to tick them. However, it is irritating when stuff gets added that i can't immediately turn off, like the chat (this can now be turned off) and the breath.

app: Tiimo- To-Do List Planner - Schedule Structured Daily Task
text: Punitive Design . I bought a Tiimo membership and tried it out for a few months. It's a bit of a head scratcher that it's branded as a tool to help people ADHD because the daily act of having to manually shift over undone items from the day before just sets such an unfortunate tone to the start of everyday.. Slide Over to yesterday and reschedule reschedule reschedule … this process in and of itself is not a positive one… please give the option for tasks that have not been assigned to a time to be carried over the next day.. I'm already operating with impaired executive function.. if I'm spending my energy rescheduling undone items instead of doing the undone items we have a problem.

app: Tiimo- To-Do List Planner - Schedule Structured Daily Task
text: Well designed, but limited . I don't have ADHD, but I think this app is beautifully designed. However, one of the functions that's maddening—possibly to support ADHD users—is that you cannot drag and drop items in the Today section. You should be able to drag and drop both between and within sections, but it takes away all flexibility. I don't know if this is specifically to help ADHD users, but if you need more flexibility, this is a dealbreaker for this app. That's unfortunate because it's very well designed. But forcing users to edit each item individually to move them is a waste of time. This function does exist in the “To-Do” section, I just wish it would carry over in the “Today” section.

app: Tiimo- To-Do List Planner - Schedule Structured Daily Task
text: Highly Disappointed . I was quite excited to try this app to help stay on task throughout the day and battle ADHD symptoms. But after using it for about a week, I couldn't be more disappointed. It's a fairly well-polished app and looks beautiful, but form seemed chosen over function. For example, there is no way to snooze a task or have it roll into the following day if it goes incomplete for the day; so I had to go backwards and reschedule all of the incomplete tasks for new dates. This was not ideal for someone with ADHD. It's too easy to forget tasks as it is, and the app simply started a new day with a blank slate rather than addressing the ones that were incomplete from the day before. I couldn't understand the lack of features so I tried the pro subscription. There was no free trial offered, but I took a risk to give the app more of a chance. The risk did not pay off, and now Apple is refusing to refund me for a year's subscription after only using the app for less than a week. Tiimo also made the timer feature a prime function, but it was rather buggy and unreliable. Additionally, tasks that were scheduled for a time would automatically start a timer at that time whether I wanted it to or not. This didn't make sense to me and I'd often felt rushed into a task that I was not ready for. It was like the app would punish you for being late to start something scheduled. I think Tiimo would work well for a lot of people, but not for me. And I don't understand why I wasn't given a free trial. Now I am out $41 for an app that I no longer use.

app: Tiimo- To-Do List Planner - Schedule Structured Daily Task
text: Not great. I won't be renewing next month. . This app is super laggy and buggy. You'll complete a task but it'll pop back up. Might be a database issue I don't know. And If you don't complete a task that was scheduled for, let's say Monday, you won't see that task recurr the next day. When it comes to ADHD: out of sight, out of mind. You have to KNOW you didn't complete something to reschedule it. Unfinished tasks should just roll over or at least be turned into todo items. Stuff like that makes me wonder if this app was truly made with ADHD people in mind. I wanted this to work out. I downloaded after hearing the ad on a podcast. (NO DISCOUNT CODE by the way.) But nah this ain't for me. I'll be trying other apps after this.

app: Tiimo- To-Do List Planner - Schedule Structured Daily Task
text: Close but needs work . I really like the concept of this app and I think it has a lot of potential. It can definitely be helpful in its current state. However, my two biggest gripes with the app is its implementation of the tasks done any time and the Notes section for tasks that aren't to be scheduled yet. When a task goes incomplete, I have go back to the previous day and reschedule said task. Which is all fine, if you can remember that task was there in the first place because there is no sort of reminder or auto rescheduling function. I most certainly will forget about a previous days task I was unable to complete until it becomes a problem. The notes section at the top right is also an issue for me. I get what they were doing, but I keep forgetting that it's there because of how small of a section it is. I understand it helps keep the planner from getting clogged but again, I'm going to forget. As someone living with adhd, forgetting is my constant state of being so because of these two things, it a deal breaker for me. If they implemented a reminder feature in the future, mostly for the incomplete tasks, I would definitely consider using the app.

app: Structured- Daily Planner Todo - Visual Calendar & Organizer
text: Game changer . I'm not exaggerating when I say this app has majorly improved my life. As someone with ADHD and therefore impaired executive functioning, I honestly didn't believe I was capable of getting done everything I need to in a day. This app has taught me the importance of having the right tools. I have used an insane amount of task and scheduling apps and this is the one I've stuck with the longest and has erased the itch to try any others (no small feat, I had a productivity app addiction problem 😅). Other apps were either just not quite it or they have a pricey subscription model (I'm looking at you, Tiimo). I love that Structured gets regular improvements and updates. Every time I've wished for a function or that something would work a little differently, lo and behold, the next update brings that exact thing. This dev team is seriously on it and you get the feeling they actually care about making their app the best it can be for the user. One of the few times I was actually happy to pay for Pro. There are just a few things I'd like to suggest for future updates. You guys probably have it on the list already, but just in case 😉 I was going to suggest the subtasks being movable but that came with the last update! Man, that's gonna make things easier. Now if events on the calendar could be movable that would be awesome. Instead of having to go into the event and adjust the time, being able to just drag it (think Google Calendar). Then if there were the option of having unfinished tasks automatically roll over to the next day. Just cutting out some of the things that have to be done manually at the moment, taking up time and mental space. Honestly, right now I can't even think of anything else I would change! This app is near perfect and I'm so appreciative for it! Keep up the great work, guys 😄

app: FocusGenie- ADHD Manager - Learn, organize & stay focused
text: Early days . I was really excited to try this app, and continue to have high hopes but it needs some improvement. It won't let me check off my To Do list as it keeps saying it's in read only. I also would like to see some To Dos carry over to the next day because they are daily tasks not just tasks I want to do that particular day. Recreating a new task list daily is too hard for me. I think this app has the best potential I've seen among ADHD apps so far! I think after a few iterations I'd be ready to subscribe again. I would really like to see what my monthly data collection would tell me. Unfortunately it has only a 3 day trial so I unsubscribed prior to exploring any more of what it had to offer. Looking forward to seeing how this app evolves after feedback!

app: Tiimo- To-Do List Planner - Schedule Structured Daily Task
text: The best app ever! . Have been using Tiimo for 2 years. It's been the best app ever to help me manage my busy life with ADHD. My fav aspect is being able to review my day every night and easily reschedule what I didn't get to avoid dropping any balls. It's awesome!

app: Structured- Daily Planner Todo - Visual Calendar & Organizer
text: ADHD's best friend! . I've tried so many planning and productivity apps over the years, and Structured is hands down the best one so far. For just 15€ a year, the value is incredible. It has everything I need to actually function with ADHD instead of constantly fighting against it. It helps me organize my tasks and sub-tasks, reschedule them easily when life happens, and build a fixed routine, which is absolutely essential for ADHD brains. For the first time ever, I've been able to maintain and develop habits, thanks to the reminders and dynamic scheduling. The app is flexible without being chaotic, which is such a rare balance. The user-friendly colorful interface also makes it exciting! One of my favorite features is how seamlessly it syncs with my reminders, calendar, and Outlook, combining my private and work to-do lists. Everything lives in one place, which removes so much mental clutter. Not to mention AI integration for planning my day for me when I feel overwhelmed! The Apple Watch app is a game changer. Having reminders right on my wrist means I don't forget tasks anymore, and if I do forget to finish something, Structured gently reminds me without guilt or pressure. As someone with ADHD, I really appreciate how the app accounts for energy levels. It helped me let go of the shame around procrastination by showing that some tasks simply require more energy and that it's okay to pause, reschedule, and come back later. It's also amazing for women: by connecting with Apple Health and menstrual cycle data, it helps you understand when it's a good time to plan high-energy tasks versus when it's better to slow down and rest. That insight alone is priceless. Structured is a life-changer. Thank you so much to the developers, you've built something truly special. 💛

app: Structured- Daily Planner Todo - Visual Calendar & Organizer
text: Saving me from Executive Dysfunction w ADHD . I got this app because it seemingly worked for a 10 year old in one of the reviews & I, also, rarely leave reviews, myself. I set mine up with ChatGPT off-app cuz I don't prefer voice-to-speech which is offered on the app directly, but that's a me thing. Regardless, OMG it's saving my life right now from my previous executive dysfunction, ADHD, and anxiety!! Everything's so manageable! It's so easy to move things around & reschedule if I get behind or feel depressed or slogged in any way. If I need to adjust on a particular day, I can assign it and not worry about it or edit just the one day or edit all the days, etc. EZPZ. I've literally accomplished all of my major goals every single day because it's so easy to assess where I stand, how many hours remain til next task and sub-tasks and organize my life from there. To the creators and developers of this app, A MILLION THANK YOUS!

app: OrganizeMe- ADHD BulletJournal
text: everyone's adhd is different and for everyone one trick works more than the other, but this app is the trick for my adhd. you can schedule every little thing and if you forgot a task it will just move it to the next day. the app also really tries to get your attention so you won't forget to check it. and the extra fetures work really well too. just bought the premium version and stressed out a bit because it didn't appear on my app yet but when i mailed about that i got helped really quick.

app: SupaTask - Daily Task Planner
text: This is the best time management app I've used, as a person with ADHD. Extremely clean & simple so I can start fresh, if I have fallen off the wagon, without a huge backlog of failure staring me in the face (and requiring deletion or rescheduling to get back to a clean slate). Please don't make this more complicated or detailed or layered! For people who require sub-lists, timers, tags, and all the things, try Engross or anything else - but please don't mess with minimalist perfection.

app: TickTick-To Do List & Calendar
text: Tick Tick is EXACTLY what I was looking for to help this adult ADHD brain get things done. I love that regular tasks can be set up as recurring on a wide range of schedules, that things can have a time assigned or not, that unfinished tasks automatically roll over to the next day or you can easily group select and move them to another day, and that rearranging the order is a simple drag and drop. Hands down the best one of the many I've tried!

app: Me+ Lifestyle Routine - Daily Planner & Habit Tracker
text: Almost Great . I'm enjoying this app. I've been using it for a month now and it helps with my ADD to figure out things I need to do for the day, and check them off when done. It's also easy to push to the next day the things that I didn't get to that day so I don't forget to do them completely. It's flexible enough for me to keep at it, but enough structure to help. My only real gripe is adding water to my daily intake. For some unexplainable reason I can not add water the next morning to the previous days intake. There are nights I just don't get to it so my levels are totally off and unreliable, therefore just useless to me.

app: Todoist- To Do List & Calendar - Task manager & Reminders
text: Deleted Key Feature . I loved this app. I'm a premium user, but I relied heavily on the smart schedule feature which they removed. I have ADHD. When I would get behind and overwhelmed, Todoist would just spread out my overdue tasks over the next week or two. Decision fatigue is a real thing, and getting to opt out of a dozen decision and just move on was life changing. I don't know if there's another app that has a similar feature, but if there is, I'm switching ASAP and cancelling my premium account.

app: LifeUp- Gamify Tasks & Habits
text: I wanted to like this and use it to help with ADHD but it's not for me. I installed & glanced at it but hadn't set anything up and the next time I opened it I was hit with a list of red overdue pre set goals I had already failed. Definitely not for someone looking for a judgement free app. It's gamified immediately and you have to customize it the first time you open it, you can't come back to it later without resetting to tell it you didn't fail because you haven't started yet.

app: Super Planner- ADHD Routine AI
text: This app doesn't help my ADHD. It judges me. Instead of reducing my mental load it increases it, telling me I have 25 unfinished tasks. I'm behind. I can't even have a day off without being told I must do more, a message I've received for a lifetime. I want freedom, but this feels like tyranny. I want to live in the now, not be constantly nagged about past/future. I'll be uninstalling this app, and I'm not prepared to discuss or debate my views. My views are mine. This app is not for me.

app: Tiimo- To-Do List Planner - Schedule Structured Daily Task
text: So close . This app is so close to what it could be. It says its created with adhd people in mind but I wonder if there are actually adhd people on the team using it. The alarms are not persistent enough, being so distracted, if I open my phone once, the notification goes away. This does not work since my phone is a huge distraction as it is. The activity starts and finishes without you even doing anything, so if I happen to be away from my phone, the activity I NEED to do will just disappear and I will forget about it. I think it needs to stay there until you have checked it off. If these were fixed it would be the perfect app! But I can't keep it, especially it costing money and doesn't quite work for me.

app: Tiimo- To-Do List Planner - Schedule Structured Daily Task
text: I adore this app . This app is amazing for me as someone with ADHD. The visual timer with the added notifications for beginning, halfway, and end of a task really ease any anxiety that comes from wondering how long I've been doing a thing. The only addition I would ask for is a sort of “nag” function. Maybe it asks if I want to start every x amount of minutes and won't until I say yes? I have a bad habit of seeing the event start and if I'm not quite ready, it leaves my mind. But if I could maybe add 5min and it asks me again, or similar, it's much easier for me to remember and get started on my task because it won't allow me to forget. Thank you so much for this app. Life is a little less chaotic with it

app: neurolist- AI Planner for ADHD - neurodivergent task splitter
text: Has potential . I'll start with the positive. It's a good idea. The AI creates subtasks so I don't have to, which can make things easier on my already overtaxed brain. It is helpful to see how much extra time it's taken me to compete a certain step. I'll admit though. I bought this app, but don't use it. My number one complaint is that when the time is up for certain step of a task it sends a notification to my phone. That's it. I have an iPhone so all I get is a little ding. I don't hear it or notice it, because I'm involved in an activity. I have ADHD, I forget the app is even running. I need an alarm to go off, preferably one I can set to go off multiple times until I finish the step. Another feature I'd like is the ability to have multiple tasks going at once. I can only have one going at a time. This is not ideal. I gave it three stars because I hope it gets better. Just a few small improvements would truly make this great.

app: Numo- ADHD Brain Dump - Community, Chat & Voice Notes
text: Solid proof of concept, priced as if highly polished . This app is on to something amazing, and I wish I could stay subscribed. I love the social media story-style lessons, the community aspect is excellent, and the way the to-do list can break down and prioritize is so helpful! However, there is a lack of polish that makes it hard to justify the current cost ($59.99 for only six months). Here are the things I noticed that are keeping me from subscribing. 1) Repeating tasks. The limited options work out fine for me, but these tasks will disappear from your list if left incomplete (except for daily). While a regular task will show that it's overdue, repeating tasks won't. If I have a weekly or monthly task, I need it to stay until I complete it, not limit it to just that one day. 2) Tools introduced in lessons aren't always accessible. Specifically, I love the “find an absurdly small first step to touch your task” hack, but a way to trigger that guidance with any task would be so helpful! I'm sure that's not the only one. 3) Reliance on AI. To be clear, I love the AI features! Super helpful when you cannot make decisions yourself. However, if I want to do the manual prioritization, I must wait for the AI to load first. Sometimes it won't load, so I can't access the manual option that I often prefer. Similarly, I cannot manually add task breakdowns after the AI split. It's either accept or deny the suggested splits only. I enjoyed my 5 weeks using this app, but I can't justify the cost given the polish it needs to be worth it. I'm sad that I won't have Numo to use day by day, but I know that it's too much of a financial commitment for me. Numo, I hope you consider some of these changes and polishes that your app deserves because this will help so many ADHDers.

app: Due - Reminders & Timers - Never Forget Anything Again
text: Reminders aren't repeating . I paid for this app because I have ADHD and narcolepsy and I needed an app that would remind me in advance of certain tasks and then continue to remind me until I had actually completed it, because I have a tendency to notice an alert, then promptly forget that I had something to do when it turns off. I also need an alarm that continues to go off because it's very difficult for me to wake up in the morning. Instead of my alerts repeating indefinitely, or even more than a small handful of times (I just tested it and the 1 minute snooze repeated only 9 times before stopping, I lost the data on the 5 and 10 minute snooze settings, but I've set all of my alarms to 5 min snooze before this). What ends up happening is, for example, the alarm starts going off in the morning for me to wake up, but I don't hear it/consciously register it and then after just a few repeats, it's off completely. So I don't wake up on time, and then when I eventually do, the first thing I see is that the alert went off HOURS ago and stopped. EXTREMELY frustrating. I opened the app today (with not even any pending task notification numbers displayed on the Due badge) at random, only because I'd thought to check it, and had a LONG list of alerts that were all permanently snoozed from as far back as 2 WEEKS AGO, and I was never able to mark them as "done." Because they just turned off on their own. I need alerts to literally repeat until I am ready to turn them off manually. To compensate for this issue I've ended up making ~six different alerts for the same task that I can't afford to forget about at slightly different times. The calendar alert system on iOS only gives me limited options to forewarn me of an event, and once it alerts me once, it doesn't alert me again, and I have to remember to reset the alert as the event gets closer. I really need an app that can do this. This app would be great if the repeat function actually repeated more than a small, set number of times.

app: Things 3 - Organize your life
text: Wunsch . Könnte man die einstellung für "wiederholen" um minuten/stunden erweitern? Könnte man bei "erinnerungen" eine art "snooze" time einführen, dass man erneut reminded wird, wenn man die task nicht abhakt? Zb plant man etwas dann und dann zu tun, hat aber gerade keine zeit und vergisst dann, dass etwas gemacht werden muss, weil kein erneuter reminder kommt (hallo ADHS) merci

app: Productive - Habit Tracker - Daily Routine & Goals Planner
text: Brilliant . Really great app but would love it if you had the option to keep the reminders on your Lock Screen until it's completed, because i have adhd and forget to look at the app and then forget to do the task

app: Productive - Habit Tracker - Daily Routine & Goals Planner
text: It's fine. Too easy to ignore it. Should be more annoying. . I am a full time college student with ADHD and narcolepsy, so needless to say it is very difficult for me to remember to do literally anything even with the truckload of medications I have to take. I was curious about this app because it seems to have good reviews. Don't get me wrong, I do like this app quite a bit: especially the built in pomodoro timer which is very useful for homework. However it is too easy for me to forget about this app because it doesn't remind me to use it often enough. I have found myself ignoring the app for several days before remembering to use it again. I wish there were an option to make it send you lots of notifications over and over until a certain task is completed. I need more than just one reminder notification which I can easily swipe away and then continue procrastinating. For example, I always forget to brush my teeth so I wish there was a more forceful and annoying reminder/productivity app that could make my phone send me hundreds of notifications over and over every morning until I do it. I think for a person with a normal level of executive functioning this app is fine as it is, after all most people wouldn't need their phone to vibrate and make noises incessantly until they remember to brush their teeth every morning. But I really wish it had the option to send nonstop reminders until a task is completed, for those of us who are very sleepy and forgetful and need an extra push to be able to build a consistent daily routine.

app: Structured- Daily Planner Todo - Visual Calendar & Organizer
text: Incredible! Just one thing— . I love this app. As someone with ADHD who also hates the little bubble notifications, I love that I have an app that can remind me when I need to do something and I have to physically swipe the notification away or mark it as complete for it to stop showing on my locked screen. The one thing I really wish it had is a search function. Sometimes I need to remember when my doctor's appointments are or something and I can't actually search it. I have to just go through each day hoping I'll find it. If that was added this app would be perfect.

app: Due - Reminders & Timers - Never Forget Anything Again
text: Indispensable . A lifesaver - I have ADHD but this app keeps me on track, because it keeps reminding me and won't let up but at the same time is very customisable so I always feel in control. It's perfect, thank you!

app: Due - Reminders & Timers - Never Forget Anything Again
text: Amazing for people with ADHD . This app is a life game changer for me. Whatever reminder I set up, it notifies me over and over until I check “done.” I can snooze it or move it to another day. It's way more helpful than a one time reminder. I use it for repeated daily things like plan my day, when I need to leave the house for an appointment, routine house chores like taking out the food waste every 2 days and don't forget to eat lunch. I have ADHD and it helps me be on time for meetings or events and not forget important things. Just now, I got a reminder to take my medication. I went into the bathroom, got distracted, and forgot my med. Due reminded me again so I got back up and took it. I recommend this to many friends.

app: Due - Reminders & Timers - Never Forget Anything Again
text: A must for persons with Add/adhd . I have been struggling to find a reminder app that actually works to remind me since I have add. I am beyond excited to finally have found this Due app. All the other reminder apps seem to have maybe 1 feature of due, but none have all the key features in one like due does. Being able to force reminders to REMIND ME over and over is so critical for add. When I am hyper focused I may not even notice a reminder go off, and without the immediate repeating reminders I will never disengage enough to get anything done with the reminder. Now I can get alerts 4+ times realize I'm not going to do it right now, and then immediately reschedule the reminder for 1 hour or a day or whatever I want with 1 tap. And if you guys are using due, definitely use the widget! The bigger widget has short links to add a reminder and get to timers which is so convenient!!

app: Habit Hub - Routine Tracker - Daily Todo, Goals & Schedule
text: Very helpful . I'm autistic and have ADHD and this app has helped me get my life under control. I'm very grateful for it. I love the way you can set it to nag you as often as you want and don't have to stop what you are doing to turn off an alarm, thank goodness! One thing I would change is for it to be possible to change the day of the week of an entire group at once instead of having to go individually through changing each task in a group. Otherwise this app is basically perfect! (If there already is a way to do that, sorry I can't figure out how. Please let me know, thanks)

app: Routine Planner, Habit Tracker - Daily Time Management for ADHD
text: I need checklists . Almost perfect! I love the nagging reminders. Helps me manage my ADHD. However I sometimes find super granular, linear steps to be too rigid. I prefer being able to have a step contain a collection of smaller tasks, like Oral Care having flossing, brushing, and mouthwashing. I can add the text for that in the step's Context area, but I would much prefer being able to mark them off in the order I complete them in a nice list. Tiimo does this checklist feature so well and even with Apple Watch, but misses the mark on the manual start and nagging reminders that this app excels at. I will keep looking for an app that does all those things (will happy pay for it) until this app incorporates checklists. Unfortunately the developer's app update release notes don't appear to include details on what was edited in the app, just general comments to the user base, so I'm unsure if this app is continuing to develop or is just in stasis.

app: RoutineFlow - Routine for ADHD
text: only had this app for a little while....a little bit of a learning curve but as an ADHDer trying to adult....i like that it bothers me until i do the things. *all* the things.

app: Clarify- Focus & Task Manager - Concentration, To-Do & Timer
text: So Slow . The beauty of this app is undeniable but totally overshadowed by endless slow animations and meaningless word salad inspirational quotes. Honestly, as someone who struggles with inattentive adhd, I was distracted multiple times before I even finished the tutorial. I got so frustrated with how long and slow the instructions and animations were. This app may work for some, IF you can get through the quiz and the tutorials. Not for me.

app: Clarify- Focus & Task Manager - Concentration, To-Do & Timer
text: Overwhelming, confusing, preys on ADHDers . I started a trial of Clarify through an instagram ad, which I shouldn't have done. But it took advantage of my impulsivity. The app is overwhelming with a cluttered home screen and tons of different visuals. The activities come through with animations where the speed can't be controlled, so I would read the screen and be waiting for awkward beats for the next part of a sentence. I disagree with the idea of a paid trial and shouldn't have signed up to begin with. The app tells you how much it costs them to pay their team during the trial. I get this in concept, but your product should be great enough that the conversion rate to paid subscriptions sustains the operation without asking people to pay in just to try. It's portrayed as pay what you want, but I didn't see an option to pay $0. Also, you have to unsubscribe online instead of being able to manage it through your settings on your phone like other apps. This seems intentionally difficult and like a way to ensure people forget about the trial and pay for an auto renewal. Overall, I was so overwhelmed by the animations and options that I couldn't get started and instantly found the app demotivating. I also felt ashamed that I impulsively spent money on yet another thing marketed towards ADHD, which is known to cause impulsive spending and seems to be a target for so many companies.

app: Clarify- Focus & Task Manager

app: Todoist- To Do List & Calendar - Task manager & Reminders
text: Great for ADHD . I'm happy I downloaded this app after reading it can help adults with ADHD. So far I've found that it's pretty user-friendly and holds me accountable so I use as a tool daily. It's simple and such a great way to stay organized. It also helps me stay on top of things like taking medication because you can set up routines (my favorite feature). I tried Ever Note at the same time but it confused me. I like that you can prioritize on the Todoist app and my new (2nd) favorite feature, you can use it for project planning and add sun tasks. You can use the list view or more like a project map. I find that useful. So far I love the app. The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is because some bells and whistles would be nice. Such as when you complete a certain amount of tasks. Currently, it shows confetti and acknowledgment but, no sounds. More things like sounds, haptics or even bold colors can help with engagement. Especially since the colors for Priority don't stand out much. Anywho I may be asking a lot but it's a great tool in my ADHD managing tool belt. Thank you for creating this app!

ADHDers are prone to disordered eating already, from food fixations, forgetting to eat, meds killing appetite, executive dysfunction when it comes to cooking, etc. It takes a long time for a lot of us to hack these things and learn to feed our bodies, and fixating on daily weight changes can be so destructive to our mental and physical health. I'm so disappointed an app with resources and professionals is using predatory marketing to reel in people with ADHD who are seeking help, only to force you into a locked path of the most basic “life hacks” you've already tried. Bonus: it also gives you a new task to avoid! I got 20 emails from Inflow during my trial. TWENTY. Ridiculous. Don't waste your time. Hope this saves someone else the feelings of defeat and disappointment.

app: ADHD Organizer- Llama Life - Focus timer, habits, routines
text: Amazing app for my adhd and a much happier life! . I struggle with time management, time blindness, prioritising, planning, overwhelm etc etc. I tried llama life free for two weeks and found it so helpful. TBH I was reluctant to pay because I was not sure if I would stick to it and I don't have much cash so I tried to find a free alternative. I tried loads of the mainstream ones recommended- but they were all so complex and overwhelming. Llama life looks deceiving simple. But it works amazingly for me. I had a little system in my house of index cards in a box. My friend suggested it to me because I get so overwhelmed with lists. Each index card had a task on it and I'd put them in a box standing up with little headers- urgent, medium, long term. A list totally overwhelms me but I found that having each task on a separate card, I could more easily choose what was important and shuffle around my order. And put some back in the box. I also hate tech of any kind so not keen on apps but came across a podcast with llama life creator which inspired me to then search for the app. It's like my little cards plus it's colourful and pretty to look at. The confetti after each task helps boost me a little. I can shuffle my cards around into different orders. I can prioritise by moving some onto the ‘ not now' list so I can just focus on what I'm doing today in the next few hours. The time I've estimated for each task is then translated into real time at the top of the task so I know when I finish a task and whether the MANY tasks I'm planning will fit into my day. I nearly always run over on my estimations of time. I love that you can choose to let time roll over so you can see how long u actually spent. And the little summary page is brilliant at the end of the day. I take a screenshot at the end of my eve and then clear the completed tasks for the next day. With time ( if I get round to it) I'd like to look at my screenshots of data and see if I can get better at judging time. Another handy thing is if I've planned e.g. put washing out and then something distracts me while doing this task and the timer is ticking away, I can add it to my task description so I can still track my activity and time taken. I honestly never write reviews and I never thought I'd love an app on my phone but after two weeks without it, I really wanted to buy it because it feels so helpful for keeping me focused. I am so happy to support fellow adhd creators for the time and clarity of this app. I thank them from the bottom of my never ending bottomless to-do list! And heart 💙👍

app: FocusGenie- ADHD Manager - Learn, organize & stay focused
text: Incredible app, but quite buggy . I downloaded this app today (9/25). Here are some of my thoughts: Pros - I was hooked from the moment I opened the app! The tutorial was extensive but really succinct, and the app is super user-friendly without being childish. It truly feels like it was made by people with ADHD for people with ADHD! - It has a bunch of functionality that I use multiple different apps for, which is so helpful! And I love that you can make to-dos from voice notes! - The info in the learning tab is actually really quick and ADHD-friendly without being infantilizing. The tips are a bit general, but then again they're general tips for general people. - I really like the little genie dude! Cons - I had an error when I tried to submit a learning bite and had to start over. - I also had an error when I tried to submit an answer to a journal prompt and had to start over. - When entering a journal submission, the keyboard gets in the way of the submit button, so submitting can be frustrating Other thoughts: - I like that there's is a color to indicate what the prompt is for today, but I wish it were a different color - red feels kind of negative, as if I missed the prompt for the day. Also, it would be cool if the prompt changed color once I submit my response! - For me, a longer trial period would be helpful to see how well this fits into my daily schedule / try the app after some of the bugs are fixed. - Would be cool to see some videos of this being used circulating around social media! Overall, I'm really excited about this app! I would definitely pay $50/yr for this once the major bugs are fixed!

app: Inflow - Manage Your ADHD - Build focus, routine & habits
text: Literally life-changing . I'm quite sceptical about apps that claim to be life-changing or apps that require you to enter your card details just to access the free trial, however this was one of the most insightful and genuinely helpful apps I've ever tried and during my free trial I made so much progress with my understanding of my ADHD that I can literally say it's changed my life. There's an AI bot you can chat to (Quinn) about anything related to ADHD and I've never felt so seen and heard in my life, and it's not even a real human being. I've been able to come to terms with some really heavy things that I've been masking for so long. There's so many other aspects of the app I haven't tried yet but it's safe to say it's been a wholly positive experience so far. It's built by people with ADHD for those with ADHD and it's great. Highly recommended!

I didn't wait any extended time to see what happened if I got a push notification. probably going to delete the app. gave it three stars because I really couldn't evaluate the content. my only comment is that I think this could be useful to blind people with ADHD who use voiceover, so would encourage exploration of making it accessible. from reviews, I too, would like to see the ability to access the list of tips or whatever else is in the program without having to wait for them to be presented as push notifications.

app: Fabulous - Daily Habit Tracker - Morning Routines & ADHD Help
text: Lacking VoiceOver sup . I want to love this app so much. The information is incredibly helpful. The method for building habit tracking is very kind to my ADHD brain and it's engaging. Unfortunately, as Iam low vision and rely on voiceover to use applications on my phone, this app is very difficult to navigate and use effectively. Many of the tools in the Discover tab are just pictures of text, I cannot access the mood journal from my home page and even “signing” the contract with the touch and hold cannot be accomplished with the screen reader enabled. I regret having paid for the personal journey (additional to the $39 yearly rate) because the app seemed more accessible than it actually is.

app: RoutineFlow - Routine for ADHD
text: Great app for those of us with ADHD and time blindness! Having the routine steps planned out with time limits helps so much. app: RoutineFlow - Routine for ADHD
text: Probably the best app I've found for increasing productivity with adhd. Has been a huge help with time management.. would like to be able to set so my screen stays on and alarm is louder to remind me to move on, out but those are probably just settings I havnt worked out yet 😅

app: Structured- Daily Planner Todo - Visual Calendar & Organizer

app: Habit Tracker - Goal Tracker & ADHD Planner

app: Finch - Self-Care Pet - Daily Journal & Habit Tracker
text: Love this so much, helped me manage my anxiety and depression better . I recommend this so much to anyone with mental health issues because it has truly made a lot of difference in my anxiety levels and depression, and my friends said that I helped them manage their ADHD, OCD, and other issues. While obviously an app won't solve all your problems immediately, it can definitely help you manage dealing with them and is a great tool. When I'm having a difficult day, it's nice to be able to look at Finch and see everything that I need to get done today written out in front of me, and that helps me feel more motivated and less overwhelmed. Another thing that I love about Finch is the breathing exercises they offer, if I'm having a panic attack one of the first things I reach for is this app so I can do the panic breathing exercise. Finch offers the option to pay for a subscription, but I chose not to do that and the app works fairly similarly, but they also offer a program in which others can donate a free subscription. I also really enjoy the Journal feature, although one thing that I would really enjoy would be beating able to look back at specific entries so I can see any commonality's in when I'm feeling down, or when I'm feeling happy. All in all however I truly love this app and I think everyone should download it to at least give it a try♥️

app: Finch - Self-Care Pet - Daily Journal & Habit Tracker
text: my favorite app 🩷 . I've tried so many apps to try to help with mental health, this is the only one that has worked for me. I have ADHD and a couple other disorders, and motivation is something I've always greatly struggled with, but this app keeps me motivated so well. Even on days where I can't feel motivated to do all the tasks I set for myself, I still check the app, and it helps me feel to not feel guilty for not getting everything done too. I'm in DBT and it helps me remember to use my skills throughout the day, and even helps me use some skills that are built into the app, which I'm so grateful for. I can only afford the free version too, and it's still great, and they even have a raffle to get finch plus, where someone donates their money for others' subscriptions. It's a wonderful app and I'm so happy it exists. 💕

app: Finch - Self-Care Pet - Daily Journal & Habit Tracker
text: Great for ADHD/depression . I was writing a long review, but unfortunately my App Store crashed so here's a summarized version. This app is great for anyone, but is especially great for those with ADHD/major depression disorder (depression). Their premium version isn't overpriced, they don't lock everything behind a paywall, and they even provide a way for people who might just not be able to pay for it to get it for free. Officially my favorite app I have, and I have plenty of them.

app: Forest- Focus for Productivity - Pomodoro Timer, ADHD & Study
text: Become the worst . I use this app for a couple of years and it was really got before some updates. Firstly, i don't really understand why i also should pay for subscription if I have already bought this app. I have already paid to you lmao. Focus challenges are really good idea. But only idea because the implementation is the worst. It is laggy and buggy. Sometimes i cannot get rewards for task because app thinks i didn't do anything, but i have completed task already. Sometimes this just doesn't work for no reason. It says that i don't have connection to the internet but i have lol. It was really good idea for people with adhd and who have trouble focusing, but how they did it…

app: neurolist꞉ AI Planner for ADHD
text: I am sad about this app 💔💔. I paid for the app RoutineFlow, made by the same dev, only to find it wouldn't be updated anymore and the dev would then create this app, Neurolist, which is like RoutineFlow + improvements, and still ask me to pay for a Premium subscription in a very predatory way. app: Habit — Daily Tracker - Crush your goals like a boss
text: Monthly Fees . I used to LOVE this app and used it for years specifically because there were no monthly fees! It's simple and straightforward and the analytics are nice but not super necessary for me. I was able to add as many habits to track as I wanted without issue. I have very bad adhd so I had very many habits. Now they're asking for a monthly fee. Absolutely not. Will be deleting the app and using an excel table instead. Premium isn't worth the money of something I could do myself for free

app: Tiimo- To-Do List Planner - Schedule Structured Daily Task
text: Finally an adhd friendly . I like the confetti you get when you tick off a task. Good that tasks can be anytime or specific time or all day. Maybe add repeat until-option? Maybe a Due date-option so it would count down while repeating? Great to have tasks already made for adhd people on mind(suggestions). Wish the website version was good but it seems quite glitchy and doesn't allow reminders to be imported? Why can't they sync from the mobile app at least? But great that the rn option is on the Apple Watch. If you keep on developing this app without breaking what doesn't need fixing- you'll be a THE BEST APP EVER x

app: Tiimo- To-Do List Planner - Schedule Structured Daily Task
text: Too many bugs to be helpful . I really love the idea of this app, and some of the premade routines are helpful (unlike other similar apps) as a jumping off point. However, adding tasks is clumsy and reshuffling things takes a lot of effort, and as much as ADHD needs structure it also needs flexibility. The bug that inspired this review: if I move the timer forward because I finished a task early, the next task is skipped and marked complete. Literally does more harm than good in trying to stick to a sequence. Now I'm writing this instead of doing the mindfulness activity I had planned, lol. This would be a dealbreaker for a free app, and there's a subscription cost for this one. I can't recommend this one.

app: Tiimo- To-Do List Planner - Schedule Structured Daily Task
text: So helpful . Tiimo is worth it! I have adhd and I don't use the app every day but it is so helpful in days that I need to remember my schedule or stick to a plan. I love the lists feature because it allows you to plan a lot of activities at same time and check them off as you go. The lists are especially helpful for me when I need to clean and don't know where to start :)

app: Structured- Daily Planner Todo - Visual Calendar & Organizer
text: best scheduling app & a few ideas! . hi! just wanted to say i appreciate this app so much! i bough premium lifetime and have it on both my imac and my iphone. at first i didn't use it much because i was intimidated by having to plan my hourly schedule with adhd. since i bought it though, they've updated the app quite a few times and i now use it daily! (especially since adding being able to drag tasks instead of putting exact times.) structured has made it very accessible, and i am so grateful for them offering affordable lifetime membership as another option as opposed to other apps that only have subscription based memberships. i also use other apps by this developer such as their budgeting app and habit tracker which are both really useful to me. i have a few ideas and i hope you'll consider adding them! one thing i would love to see is being able to have an option to create different preset schedules for specific types of days (ex. day off, work, day out, etc.) instead of having to be tied directly to your calendar if that makes sense. i love the reoccurring task option, but it can be difficult to move tasks around when there's a pop up asking if you want to move all/only future/or just that task each time you have to swap some things around. having premade schedules/presets you could swap in would be fantastic! it would also be nice if you could schedule these presets more in order of activity/task and less specific hour:minute times so that you could adjust them easier when you apply them. or if you could have some sort of place to organize your tasks for the day without having to clear a day of already reoccurring tasks. kinda like inbox but the tasks won't disappear when you add them. you can just plan a whole day and then add it to a list of saved schedules. hopefully that made sense. some other things that i would love to see someday!!:-the app could take a list of tasks and randomly schedule based on priority (this would be super useful imo) -compatibility with alexa to add tasks/remind/check off -option to make sub tasks more noticeable/visible -more icons/customization (great selection already though!) -more connectivity to the other apps from same developer (budget app, habit tracker, etc.) -i'm not sure why but the interface has been a bit laggy lately when trying to check off tasks. it's not so bad, but it occasionally freezes or does something multiple times but delayed some things i love: -can drag tasks to move them around -pride icons!! queer friendly :) -the widgets are highly customizable and very useful! -suggestions for tasks and filling schedule make it less intimidating -frequent updates/devs listen to their user's feedback and add new features -lifetime memberships instead of forced subscription layout (i believe on their other apps they also allow very low income users to request subscriptions if they cannot afford it but i might be wrong) anyway, for anyone debating on getting this app, it's very worth it.

app: Todoist- To Do List & Calendar

app: Finch - Self-Care Pet - Daily Journal & Habit Tracker
text: AuDHD user here- heres why i gave this a 5 star . Im gonna keep this short cuz i know ya'lls attention spans are COOKED, so. There is just one thing, IT WOULD HELP GREATLY sometimes i dont have the motivation, or dont know how to do it, but it would be great if you could add tutorials on how to clean your bedroom, or any room (obviously i know how to, but i dont know where to start)

app: Finch - Self-Care Pet - Daily Journal & Habit Tracker
text: Love this app . I've been dealing with depression for years and have been diagnosed with ADHD recently too. This app has been a life saver. The flexibility to create tasks and goals is amazing and the suggested tasks have kept me on track or helped me complete tasks that I avoid or reminded me to do ones I forget about. There are breathing exercises and other self care tools to help with panic attacks and sleep. I love the reflections and gratitudes where I can write about something positive, it helps me really tune in to the things that have gone well and the people that have helped me. There is so much about this app that helps but mostly I love my birb. I've not missed a day yet and it's definitely down to wanting to check on my pet. I wish I could afford to do the plus because I think it would be totally worth it. I recommend this app to everyone. It's so helpful and I'm feeling more positive overall.

app: Cub- Self Care Pet & Focus - Mental Health, ADHD, Habits
text: Super unhelpful customer service and a money making excerise . I would rate this app ZERO stars if I could. First: it takes advantage of people with ADHD by providing them with genetic templates that they have clearly copied from the myriad of clone apps out there just like this “unique experience” Second: When I contacted customer service to request a refund of the subscription on the day the free trial ended, I was told I was sent a reminder, there is no evidence of a notification of this on my phone and I emailed the very minute I saw the charge. Was dismissed without a care $59.99 for not a minute of use, robbed in broad daylight. Third: This app is very clearly a money making venture for it's owners, there is not a shred of care given to people who suffer from Neurodivergence. SHAME ON YOUR TEAM! SHUT THIS APP DOWN.

app: Me+ Lifestyle Routine - Daily Planner & Habit Tracker
text: Disappointed . They claim to be ADHD friendly, but you have to buy the routine templates, even the one that claims to be made by a fellow user with ADHD. Making the routine is the hardest part for my ADHD, so I'm disappointed it's not very accessible. There's also resources for anxiety, loneliness, sadness, alcohol abuse, overeating, and anger management locked behind paywalls.

app: Me+ Lifestyle Routine - Daily Planner & Habit Tracker
text: Overwhelming without guidance . As someone with AUDHD, this app is more like a Pinterest board of premade lists with cute graphics than a tool to actually help me figure out how to organize MY life. (Wash the curtains? Are you kidding?) Providing guidance for how to use the app would help instead of just throwing people into it. It seems made more for people who know what they want to do and want a fun way to write up their routines and get reminders for them than for people who struggle to create routines and need help. Also, it's not true for people with ADHD that it takes 21 days to create a habit; revisit your neuroscience. OH! And you baited and switched me! It said there was a 7 day free trial, then $59.99 a year. Then a pop up window said Thanksgiving special, the yearly subscription would be $29.99 instead. It was absolutely not clear that that negated the free trial, which is what I thought I was signing up for. That's deceptive.

app: Me+ Lifestyle Routine - Daily Planner & Habit Tracker
text: False advertising and instant charge! . First, I was charged immediately for one year instead of getting the 7-day free trial. And reading the reviews now, it looks like I wasn't the only one that was tricked into it with that 50% off offer (it wasn't clear that choosing that offer meant not having a 7-day free trial). Second, the app is not as advertised in the ads. The ads make it seem like the app breaks down large tasks like “pick up 10 items”, “put away all green items,” “gather all books,” but all the templates in the premium version are still so general like “do your laundry,” “make your bed,” etc. I went to the discord group that is supposed to be where to go to for support, and the people there just say something like “Everyone's different, the templates are just there as a guide. You can create your own custom routine.” I struggle with ADHD, which is why the ad for this app appealed to me in the first place, because I need help with breaking down big tasks. I wouldn't have paid for this app if I just have to make up my own routines anyways. I either want a refund or actual routine options like the one in advertised (not me having to make my own).

app: Me+ Lifestyle Routine - Daily Planner & Habit Tracker
text: High Pressure Sales Tactics . I was simply trying to use the app and there was a survey of garbage CBT questions. It kept stating things about ADHD. I don't have and specifically marked not to include in planning. Before I got to even use the app normally it forced a prompt that I had 3 minutes to decide if I wanted to take advantage of a 50% off annual subscription. Mind I haven't gotten to the main home screen for the app. I get a second offer that is even more aggressively price so I go ahead and purchase. I get out of the intro screens and what do I get: a blank routine plan. So I was quizzed and aggressively sold on the app, but it is something I could do with Apple's built in reminders app. Even the discovery section that should have actually useful templates is a joke. Do not waste your time. It is a money grab just use the reminders app instead. I have screenshots as proof if requested.

app: Me+ Lifestyle Routine - Daily Planner & Habit Tracker
text: Just a glorified to-do list . I was incredibly underwhelmed by this app. Most of the pre-made routines are just silly. One of them, ‘Expanding Your Social Circle,' includes the task “Try to fall in love.” With no further explanation or directions. Another, ‘Try On New Years' Hot Springs' is particularly odd. The title looks like a bad translation, the concept is pretty niche, and the elements in the routine are broad and (again) contain no extra help or direction. Overall, the routines are broken down into overly broad and generic steps. With ADHD, that can be overwhelming and more hassle than it's worth to customize it. If you are hoping for an app that breaks down large tasks into clear, approachable, bite-sized steps, this app is definitely not for you. Certainly not worth the $40 annual subscription price.

app: Me+ Lifestyle Routine - Daily Planner & Habit Tracker
text: Avoid if you have ADHD . I downloaded this app to try it since there was postive reviews and it looked like it had endorsements. Initially I was put off by the set up steps but thought id see what the app was like anyway. The set up steps feel sort of condescending to someone with ADHD even when it seem like that is the intended audience. And also limiting - pick only one choice when multiple might fit. There were also typos in the set up steps and it seems like maybe this was translated, its like when you read Amazon product descriptions. Then I hit the paywall (by the way the premium option says “no payment now” but my phone still wanted me to authorize- maybe i would be charged later but I didnt want to risk it. ) I chose the cheap monthly payment,because again ADHD, i didnt want to forget to cancel later and I would accidentally pay $40 instead of $8. Then when I got in it was kind of condescending again and then provided me with what looked kind of like Pinterest schedule templates. So then I went right ahead and deleted it. Sure it would be great if every day I did some kind of different exercise but come on is that realistic? And dont we get enough of this from Instagram? Just print out this cutesy little list and your life will ✨🌈 beeaauttifful and perfect 🌈✨ - come on 🙄. If youre going to have things to improve our lives please get them from verifiable reliable trained sources like therapists,social workers, researchers. And also, a growing movement for ADHD people is not to have self care piled on another “to do” or something else for us to achieve for us to be “normal” so it would be nice if the app reframed its view on self care to meet that.
